description: Well-known identifiers for intent.architecturalPatterns[]. Producers SHOULD use one of these IDs when the named pattern applies; for project-specific patterns not in this registry, use the 'x:' prefix. Advisory, not schema-enforced (intent.architecturalPatterns is an open string array).

entries.name: Circuit breaker
entries.summary: Stops calling a failing dependency after a threshold of errors, failing fast until it recovers, to prevent cascading failure and resource exhaustion.

entries.name: Bulkhead
entries.summary: Partitions resources (thread pools, connection pools) so a failure or overload in one partition cannot exhaust resources needed by others.

entries.name: Timeout
entries.summary: Bounds how long a caller waits on a dependency so a slow or hung call cannot block indefinitely.

entries.name: Fail fast
entries.summary: Rejects work early when preconditions (capacity, dependency health) are not met, rather than accepting it and failing partway.

entries.name: Retry with backoff
entries.summary: Retries a transient failure with increasing delay and jitter to recover without amplifying load or synchronizing retries into a thundering herd.
entries.cite: AWS Architecture Blog; Nygard, Release It!.

entries.name: Fallback
entries.summary: Serves a degraded but acceptable response (cached data, default, reduced feature) when the primary path is unavailable.

entries.name: Command Query Responsibility Segregation
entries.summary: Separates the write model from one or more read models so each can be scaled and optimized independently.

entries.name: Event sourcing
entries.summary: Persists state as an append-only log of events; current state is derived by replaying them, giving a full audit trail and temporal queries.

entries.name: Cache-aside
entries.summary: The application loads on a cache miss and populates the cache; the cache is not in the write path. Also called lazy loading.

entries.name: Write-through cache
entries.summary: Writes go to the cache and the backing store synchronously, keeping the cache consistent at the cost of write latency.

entries.name: Write-back cache
entries.summary: Writes go to the cache and are flushed to the backing store asynchronously, lowering write latency at the risk of loss on failure before flush.

entries.name: Saga
entries.summary: Coordinates a long-running business transaction as a sequence of local transactions with compensating actions for rollback, avoiding distributed locks.

entries.name: Transactional outbox
entries.summary: Writes an outgoing message to an outbox table in the same local transaction as the state change, then relays it, guaranteeing at-least-once delivery without a distributed transaction.

entries.name: Unit of Work
entries.summary: Tracks the objects changed during a business transaction and coordinates writing them out and resolving concurrency as one commit.
entries.cite: Fowler, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture.

entries.name: Repository
entries.summary: Mediates between the domain and data-mapping layers behind a collection-like interface, decoupling business logic from persistence.
entries.cite: Fowler, Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture.
